source_user: Advanced cluster case RDMA-38: Explain how RDMA changes the data path for multi-node GPU training or inference. Variant 38 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: separate verbs, queues, memory registration, transport selection, bandwidth, latency, and fallback behavior; compare measured device counters with application-level communication time. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer: For Variant 38 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition., state the recorded assumptions before making claims. Assume the GPU workload, rank topology, NIC and link, GPU-direct support, drivers, framework/collective library, transport mode, and fallback policy are explicitly recorded; do not infer platform facts. Trace the operation from the application collective or point-to-point call through the communication library, RDMA verbs objects (queue pairs, work requests, completions), registered memory and permissions, NIC/link, and remote host or GPU buffer. State whether the path is GPU-direct or host-staged and what configuration or error causes fallback. Compare with a named non-RDMA baseline using the same message-size and batch/parallelism distributions, topology cases, warm-up, steady-state window, repetitions, clock source, and units. Measure end-to-end step time, communication and overlap time, throughput, latency percentiles, CPU use, completion/error counters, retries/link events where available, and device counters; correlate timestamps but do not treat counters as proof of application benefit. For the performance analysis, report distributions and confidence intervals or bootstrap uncertainty, separate steady state from warm-up, and explain bandwidth/latency units and overlap accounting. Define the falsifiable hypothesis as a predeclared change in a named application metric relative to baseline, with an acceptance threshold and uncertainty; distinguish estimates from measured results. A safe procedure should preserve correctness, bound retries and recovery, and stop or roll back on an agreed error-rate, timeout, data-corruption, tail-latency, throughput, or convergence regression. Verify collective results and application outputs after each fault test, and document software/hardware versions, configuration, raw measurements, exclusions, and confounders. Evidence required before claiming improvement is repeated paired runs, correlated application traces and device/link/completion data, topology/workload coverage, and failure-injection results showing detection, bounded recovery, correctness, and rollback. Do not expose credentials or unnecessary sensitive telemetry; redact identifiers and retain only approved aggregates.

A safe procedure should preserve correctness, bound retries and recovery, and stop or roll back on an agreed error-rate, timeout, data-corruption, tail-latency, throughput, or convergence regression. Verify collective results and application outputs after each fault test, and document software/hardware versions, configuration, raw measurements, exclusions, and confounders. Evidence required before claiming improvement is repeated paired runs, correlated application traces and device/link/completion data, topology/workload coverage, and failure-injection results showing detection, bounded recovery, correctness, and rollback. Do not expose credentials or unnecessary sensitive telemetry; redact identifiers and retain only approved aggregates.
